title: Conan vs. Heiji, Deduction Battle Between the Detectives of the East and West
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shinichi, Heiji, Kazuha, Kogoro, Ran, Megure, and newly-introduced recurring character Sera Masumi) omitted by convention -- they are present across the corpus and contribute the investigative legwork/deduction but are not case-specific entities. FBI Agent Camel is kept as a person node (role: witness) since his on-scene testimony is the load-bearing evidence chain for this case, unlike the omitted core cast. Discrepancies vs. the old lower-fidelity file (cases/ep651...): (1) old file's e1 says Amakasu poisoned the company president 'years earlier' -- the transcript states it happened 'last week', a backstory murder in the immediate past, not a years-old cold case. (2) old file's e2 says a manager 'blackmails' Amakasu -- the transcript does not support blackmail; Shibamiya (the primary discoverer of the president's body, and Amakasu's childhood friend who had recommended him for the job) instead phones Amakasu at the restaurant urging him to turn himself in, which is what Amakasu silences him to prevent. (3) old file's culprit id (s2, Amakasu Tooru) is otherwise correct -- confirmed against the transcript's own deduction chain (dialect tells + handedness tell). Final ~2 minutes of the episode (letter from Wakamatsu's killer to Hattori Heiji) is a teaser/hook for the next story arc, not part of this episode's solved case; included minimally as backstory nodes since Wakamatsu is named and the letter is plot-consequential for the franchise, but no culprit is asserted for it since the sender's identity is deliberately withheld in-episode -- inventing one would violate the no-fabrication rule. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Amakasu called the salty miso soup and salt ramen 'spicy', where the other two suspects (and true Tokyoites) called the same dishes 'salty' -- a Kansai word-choice tell.
Amakasu referred to his own way of speaking as 'Tokyo dialect' -- only Kansai people label their own speech that way; a real Tokyoite wouldn't name it at all.
Amakasu held his cigarette in his left hand despite having placed his ramen chopsticks on his right -- proves he's actually right-handed and was avoiding the hand he'd touched poison with.

Camel's quoted 'confession' -- 'jibun' and 'Abe-chan' -- reread in Kansai dialect: 'jibun' means 'you' not 'me', and 'Abe-chan' was actually 'ame-chan' (candy); the line reverses from a suicide confession into Shibamiya accusing and warning Amakasu.
